scope_gaps.note: Neither snapshot advises self-monitoring of caffeine timing or sleep; the NHS page lists caffeine only as a common cause of insomnia (line 61).

The NHS page is general self-help advice for people with insomnia and shows no evidence basis for the 6-hour figure. It names alcohol and smoking in the same bullet. A reader might assume the figure is evidence-based; the sentence only says it is an NHS recommendation.

The abstract does not state the population, doses or timing of the 24 included studies. A reader might assume 8.8 h applies to everyone and to any coffee, whereas the abstract ties it to coffee at 107 mg per 250 mL and to avoiding a reduction in total sleep time only.
The abstract does not describe how 8.8 h and 13.2 h were derived from the pooled data (model or subset analysis); full text needed to see this.
The abstract gives a pooled figure only. It does not give the caffeine doses, timing or population behind the 45 minutes, so a reader might assume it applies to a typical evening coffee.

The two timing figures belong to the specific doses stated (107 mg per 250 mL coffee; 217.5 mg pre-workout serve). A reader might assume they transfer to other drinks or doses; the abstract does not say so.
The abstract does not say how the 107 mg and 217.5 mg figures were chosen (for example an assumed average content); a reader might assume they are measured values for every coffee or supplement.
